_readme: 3D printing: the intro screen, both plans, Plan B failure options, the rules, the gallery, the self-check, and phone reference mode. The `smell` failure is safety-only and always shows the fixed safety message from assistant.json.

intro.lead: Most people bring a file and our staff print it for you. It usually takes [[turnaround|3 to 5 days]].

A.title: We print it for you
A.say: “I’d like staff to 3D print a file for me.”

facts.v: Your file on [[how to bring the file|a USB drive or by email]]

steps.detail: Download a model from a trusted source such as [[trusted model sources|Printables or Thingiverse]], or bring one you made. We accept [[accepted file types|.STL, .OBJ, and .3MF files]].
steps.alt: A 3D model file open on a computer screen.

steps.text: Check that it fits the rules.
steps.detail: It has to fit within [[size limit|5 × 5 × 5 inches]] — about the size of a coffee mug[[confirm the coffee-mug comparison|]] — and print in under [[time limit|6 hours]]. Some items aren’t allowed.
steps.alt: A coffee mug next to a finished print, showing the size limit.

steps.text: Submit it [[how and where to submit|at the TechCentral desk or online]].
steps.detail: [[how to submit|Bring it to the desk on a USB drive, or fill in the 3D print request form at cpl.org/3dprint]]. Staff check every file before printing it.

steps.text: Wait for it, then pick it up.
steps.detail: It usually takes about [[turnaround|3 to 5 days]]. We’ll tell you it’s ready by [[ready notice method|email or text]] — or just ask at the desk. Pick it up within [[pickup window|14 days]]. Unclaimed prints: [[unclaimed print policy|recycled after 14 days]].
steps.alt: The pickup shelf at the TechCentral desk.

B.title: Run it yourself
B.say: “I’d like to book a 3D printer. I’ve been checked out on them.”

facts.v: [[self-service pricing|10¢ a gram, paid at the desk]]
[[how far ahead to book|Up to 7 days ahead]]
Your sliced file on [[file media|a USB drive or SD card]]

steps.text: Make sure you’re ready to run it yourself.
steps.detail: This is for people who’ve been checked out on our printers: [[the actual qualification rule|you’ve done the 3D printing orientation and one supervised print]]. If you haven’t been, staff will print it for you.
steps.alt: A staff member signing a patron off at a 3D printer.

steps.text: Book a printer [[booking method|online or at the desk]].
steps.detail: [[how to book|Book at cpl.org/tc/book or at the desk, up to 7 days ahead. A booking lasts up to 3 hours.]]

steps.text: At the machine, follow reference mode.
steps.detail: One big step at a time, on your phone or on the card beside each printer. The nozzle and bed get hot [[temperatures|— about 400°F and 140°F]]. Don’t leave a print running unattended [[unattended printing policy|— staff stop prints left alone]].
steps.alt: A patron following the reference card beside a 3D printer.

steps.text: If a print fails, check here.

fails.label: Not sticking to the bed
fails.fix: Stop the print. Clean the bed with [[bed cleaning method|an alcohol wipe from the drawer]] and check it’s level [[who levels the bed|— or ask staff to level it]]. Then start again.

fails.label: Spaghetti mess
fails.fix: Stop the print. Let the nozzle cool before you clear the plastic. Usually the first layer didn’t stick, or the model needs supports. Staff can check your file.

fails.label: Stopped partway
fails.fix: Check whether the filament ran out or tangled. Don’t restart a half-finished print on your own [[restart policy|— restarts need a staff check]] — tell staff.

rules.v: [[prohibited items list|Weapons or weapon parts, anything illegal, and replicas that could be mistaken for the real thing]]
Up to [[size limit|5 × 5 × 5 inches]] — about the size of a coffee mug[[confirm the coffee-mug comparison|]]
[[filament types and colors|PLA in 8 colors — ask to see the color board]]
Within [[pickup window|14 days]]. Unclaimed prints: [[unclaimed print policy|recycled after 14 days]]
Staff at the desk [[desk direction, two or three words|to your left]]

policy: [[official TechCentral 3D printing policy text, verbatim|SAMPLE POLICY TEXT — replace with the official policy, word for word.]]

[[policy paragraph 2|Cleveland Public Library offers 3D printing for personal, educational, and small-business use. The library may refuse any print request. Items that violate law or library policy, including weapons and weapon components, will not be printed.]]
[[policy paragraph 3|Patrons are responsible for the content of their files. Staff do not modify designs. Prints that fail because of a design problem are charged at the normal rate.]]

refSteps.text: Check the bed is clean and empty.
Load your file from [[file media|a USB drive or SD card]] on the printer’s screen.
refSteps.alt: The printer’s screen showing the file list.

refSteps.text: Check the filament: [[material|PLA]] loaded, with enough on the spool.
refSteps.alt: A spool of filament on the printer’s holder.

refSteps.text: Start the print and watch the first layer go down.
refSteps.alt: The nozzle laying down the first layer.
refSteps.safety: The nozzle and bed are hot [[temperatures|— about 400°F and 140°F]]. Don’t touch them.

refSteps.alt: A patron seated next to the printer.
refSteps.safety: Don’t leave a print running unattended [[unattended printing policy|— staff stop prints left alone]].

refSteps.text: When it’s done, wait [[cool-down time|10 minutes]] for the bed to cool, then remove your print.
refSteps.alt: A finished print being lifted off the bed.
refSteps.safety: Let the bed cool before you touch it.
